scenario: The user is swamped at work and needs help preparing a steel-coil audit their boss asked for. They uploaded several photos taken inside a plant and in a storage yard and want a careful visual count of the hot-rolled coils (without double-counting the same coils shown from different angles), a split between plant and yard, an overall total, a count of coils showing deterioration or corrosion, and the percentage that represents. why: This rubric fails. The problem is that six of the criteria demand exact counts of things that genuinely cannot be counted to a single number from the photos. The criteria insist on exactly 10 coils across the three plant photos, exactly 127 in the yard photo, exactly 137 overall, exactly 34 deteriorated coils, exactly a 24.82% deterioration rate, and the same exact 137 again in the memory note. But the yard photo is a dense, overcast wide shot where a careful person lands in a range (roughly 110 to 150), not on 127; the plant photos are blurry and rotated and the prompt itself warns the same coils may appear from different angles, so whether they overlap is a judgment call and any reasonable count differs; corrosion is a gradual, partly-hidden continuum with no precise count; and the total and percentage simply inherit all of that uncertainty. The clearest proof is that the model's own image-reading tool read the yard as 'approximately 150+, a precise count is difficult' and gave no deterioration count, and the model kept changing its own numbers (89 then 137, 11 then 34). A genuinely careful response that arrives at any other defensible count would be marked wrong by these six criteria, which is backwards: the criteria reject correct work. That is enough to fail the task. The remaining criteria (the name, the employee ID, the delivery date, the image section, and the memory-note details) are all fine and stay out of the count. The reviewer's notes on the rubric leaning light on point-deducting criteria, on test coverage, and on a scoring rationale were either advisory or outside what can fail a task, and there are no real automated tests here (the test file is just an inert block of text).
fix: Replace the exact-count criteria with tolerant ones. Instead of demanding exactly 127, 137, 34, and 24.82%, accept any count within a reasonable range that a careful reviewer would reach (for the yard, the total, the deteriorated count, and the derived percentage), or redesign the photos so the coils are individually distinguishable and countable to a single defensible number. The de-duplication criterion for the plant photos should likewise accept any reasonable reading rather than pinning one exact figure.

Remove the test requiring MATCH/MISMATCH/UNVERIFIABLE verdicts, remove the test requiring the email to mention a mismatch, and remove the test requiring the $312K/$123K/$61K valuation figures.
